bottleneck: Most common diseases — heart disease, diabetes, schizophrenia — involve dozens to thousands of variants with tiny individual effects, unknown interactions, and pleiotropic genes that influence many traits. Editing hundreds of loci simultaneously is technically impractical and biologically reckless, since gene networks, feedback loops, and developmental timing are only partly mapped. Single-gene success stories do not scale.
current_state: Polygenic risk scores predict but do not enable treatment. Multiplex editing is limited to a handful of loci in research settings, far below what polygenic disease would require.

title: Polygenic diseases resist multiplex gene editing
why_it_blocks: The diseases that kill and disable the most people are polygenic. Until editing can address many variants at once with predictable network effects, gene editing remains a therapy for rare monogenic conditions only.
